The runbook makes refunds a money movement that can't be auto-fixed, and any unexpected exception goes to payments. The routing says to decide the case as a person straight away when the runbook calls for it, so I'll run DecideCase with person and RaiseToPerson, both in one block since neither depends on the other, and skip asking the sorter because the runbook already settles it.

I'm weighing whether to mention the likely bug: the stack trace points to Api/Refund.cs line 12, where a substring call seems to get a negative index. That could help the person picking this up. I can't tell from here whether order 1005 was refunded or whether the failure came before the refund call, so I won't claim either way.

This is a refund, which moves money, and the runbook allows no automatic fix and sends every exception other than the two expected ones to payments. I'm raising it to a person now, with the order id, exception and stack location so payments can check whether the customer was refunded.

arguments.reason: The refund runbook says refund moves money, nothing is auto-fixable, and every exception other than the two expected ones goes to payments; this is a System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException for order 1005, so it goes to a person.

arguments.summary: refund for order 1005 failed with System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: "startIndex ('-4') must be a non-negative value. (Parameter 'startIndex')". The stack trace points to OrderService.OrderApi.RefundOrder in src/OrderService/Api/Refund.cs line 12, via a String.Substring call. Error timestamp 2026-11-24T12:16:18Z, service order-service, method refund.
arguments.why: Refund moves money and the runbook sends every unexpected exception to payments, so payments must check whether the customer was refunded for order 1005 before anyone retries or changes anything. No agent may change payments code, and whether money moved is unknown from this error alone.
